newsitem.title: CHINA: China's key coal mines 1996 profits up 53.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: China's key coal mines 1996 profits up 53.4 pct.

text.p: China's key state-owned coal mines registered profits of 1.55 billion yuan ($186.7 million) in 1996, up 53.4 percent from 1995, the Financial News said on Tuesday.
The newspaper did not say whether the figure was before or after tax profits.
Revenues of key state-owned coal mines totalled 38.5 billion yuan, up 15.8 percent from the previous year, the newspaper said.
China's coal output reached 1.35 billion tonnes last year, up 4.6 percent or 60 million tonnes from 1995, it said, but gave no further details.

China's coal industry is chronically inefficient, and of China's 93 key state-owned coal mines, only 55 were profitable last year. That was more than double the 26 that were profitable in 1995, officials say.
